steps.body: A sorting rule is a yes/no question you ask every shape. 'Does it have a right angle?' splits a pile into two: the yeses and the nos. The rule doesn't care about the shape's name — only whether it passes the test.

widget.prompt: Rule: 'Has at least one right (square) angle.' Sort each shape yes or no.

items.label: Square
items.feedback: A square has four right angles — easily passes the one-right-angle test.

items.label: Rectangle
items.feedback: Four square corners — a clear yes.

items.label: Triangle with no square corner
items.feedback: This triangle's corners are all tilted — no right angle, so it fails the test.

items.label: Rhombus (tilted corners)
items.feedback: A rhombus has equal sides but its corners are tilted, not square — no right angle.

widget.missFeedback: Ask ONLY the rule's question: does the shape have a square corner? Ignore everything else.
widget.successFeedback: Square and rectangle pass; the tilted-corner triangle and rhombus fail. One rule, two piles.

predict.prompt: Can a shape have a right angle without BEING a rectangle?

options.label: Yes — one square corner isn't the whole club
No — right angles mean rectangle
Only triangles are allowed to

predict.reveal: A right triangle carries a square corner and isn't remotely a rectangle — one feature satisfies one rule, not a whole definition. Sorting by a rule means checking THAT rule alone.

explanationVariants: The rule asks only about equal sides — a rhombus has four equal sides, so it lands in the YES pile even without square corners.
Sorting ignores the name: the rhombus passes the equal-sides test, so it's a yes.

widget.prompt: Rule: 'All sides equal.' Where does a rhombus go?

options.label: Yes pile — a rhombus has four equal sides
options.feedback: The rule asks only about equal sides, and the rhombus has them. It passes.

options.label: No pile — it doesn't have square corners
options.feedback: Square corners aren't the rule here — this rule is 'all sides equal,' which the rhombus passes.

options.label: Neither — a rhombus isn't a real shape
options.feedback: A rhombus is a real quadrilateral with four equal sides — so it clears this equal-sides rule.

options.label: Both piles at once
options.feedback: A yes/no rule gives ONE answer per shape. The rhombus has equal sides, so it's a yes.

steps.body: A shape can pass **more than one rule** at once. A square passes 'has a right angle' AND 'all sides equal.' When two rules overlap, the shapes that pass BOTH sit in the shared middle — like two hoops on the floor with an overlap where the double-winners stand.

explanationVariants: A square has four right angles AND four equal sides, so it passes both rules and belongs in the overlap.
Both tests come back yes for a square — it stands in the shared middle of the two hoops.

widget.prompt: Two rules: 'has a right angle' and 'all sides equal.' Which shape passes BOTH?

options.label: A square
options.feedback: Four right angles and four equal sides — a square passes both rules and sits in the overlap.

options.label: A long rectangle
options.feedback: A rectangle passes 'has a right angle' but its sides aren't all equal — so it fails the second rule and misses the overlap.

options.label: A tilted rhombus
options.feedback: A rhombus passes 'all sides equal' but has no right angle — it fails the first rule, so not the overlap.

options.label: No shape can pass two rules
options.feedback: Shapes often pass several rules. A square passes both of these at once — that's exactly the overlap.

widget.prompt: Two rules: A = 'has 4 sides', B = 'has a right angle'. Sort each shape by which rules it passes.

buckets.label: Only A (4 sides, no right angle)

items.label: Rectangle
items.feedback: Four sides (A) and right angles (B) — the overlap.

items.label: Rhombus (tilted)
items.feedback: Four sides (A ✓) but tilted corners (B ✗) — only A.

items.label: Triangle, no square corner
items.feedback: Three sides (A ✗) and no right angle (B ✗) — neither pile.

items.label: Square
items.feedback: Four sides and right angles — squarely in the overlap.

widget.missFeedback: Check each rule separately, then place the shape by the combination of yes/no answers.
widget.successFeedback: Rectangle and square pass both; the rhombus is A-only; the tilted triangle passes neither.

explanationVariants: The overlap holds shapes passing BOTH rules — a rhombus passes 'equal sides' but not 'right angle,' so it stays out of the overlap.
To reach the shared middle a shape must clear both tests; the rhombus clears only one.

widget.prompt: Rules: 'all sides equal' and 'has a right angle.' Which shape does NOT belong in the overlap?

options.label: A rhombus — it has equal sides but no right angle
options.feedback: It clears only one rule, so it stays in the equal-sides hoop but outside the shared middle.

options.label: A square — it belongs in the overlap
options.feedback: A square passes BOTH rules, so it DOES belong in the overlap. The question asks which one doesn't.

options.label: Every shape belongs in the overlap
options.feedback: Only shapes passing both rules do. A rhombus passes just one, so it's outside — it's the answer.

options.label: No shape can be in the overlap
options.feedback: A square sits right in it, passing both rules. The rhombus is the one that misses.

hints: Test each rule on its own first.
Rule 1 'four sides': does a square pass? Rule 2 'all sides equal': does it pass?
To get through the gate, a shape must pass BOTH.
explanationVariants: The gate needs 'four sides' AND 'all sides equal.' A square passes both (yes and yes); a rectangle passes the first but fails the second (unequal sides). So only the square gets through.
Both tests must be yes: square = yes/yes ✓, rectangle = yes/no ✗. The square alone clears the gate.

widget.prompt: A gate opens only for shapes with FOUR SIDES and ALL SIDES EQUAL. Which gets through: a square or a 6-by-3 rectangle?

options.label: Only the square — it passes both rules
options.feedback: Square: four sides ✓, all equal ✓. Rectangle: four sides ✓ but sides unequal ✗. The square alone passes.

options.label: Both — they each have four sides
options.feedback: Four sides is only rule one. Rule two ('all sides equal') stops the 6-by-3 rectangle — its sides differ.

options.label: Only the rectangle
options.feedback: The rectangle fails 'all sides equal' (6 ≠ 3). The square passes both rules and gets through.

options.label: Neither passes both
options.feedback: The square passes both: four equal sides with the count of four. It clears the gate.

takeaways: A sorting rule is a yes/no question asked of every shape.
A shape can pass several rules; shapes passing two overlapping rules sit in the shared middle.
For a compound rule, a shape must pass EVERY part.

concept.body: Quick rewind. A sorting rule is just a **yes/no question**. Ask it about a shape, get one answer, drop the shape in the matching pile. 'Has a right angle?' — square says yes, tilted rhombus says no. The rule ignores the shape's name entirely.

explanationVariants: A rectangle has square corners, so it answers YES to 'has a right angle.'
The right-angle test comes back yes for a rectangle — into the yes pile.

widget.prompt: Rule: 'has a right angle.' Where does a rectangle go?

options.label: Yes pile
options.feedback: Four square corners — a clear yes.

options.label: No pile
options.feedback: A rectangle's corners are all square — it passes the right-angle test, so it's a yes.

options.label: It can't be sorted
options.feedback: Every shape gets a yes or no. A rectangle has right angles — yes.
